structuralDecisions.decision: Place ReagentMapView.vue under apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/src/views/ with no new package and no new base class. Cesium viewer construction lives entirely inside the view's onMounted/onBeforeUnmount, mirroring LocationsView.vue's __SATURDAY_LEAFLET_MAP__ lifecycle (expose the seam on mount, set it to undefined on unmount). Reversibility: Cheap — one file, deletable without touching any other component.
structuralDecisions.rationale: This is purely additive within the established per-view pattern this app already uses for its other map (Leaflet). No existing abstraction needs to change, and introducing a Cesium-specific base class or composable now would be speculative — there is exactly one caller.

structuralDecisions.decision: Serve Cesium's static Build/Cesium assets under /cesium/ via a small inline Vite plugin added to vite.config.ts (configureServer for dev, closeBundle for the production build), rather than committing generated assets into public/ or adding a new build-tool dependency. This introduces a new pattern for the monorepo — no existing app here serves a third-party package's prebuilt static tree under a custom URL prefix at both dev and build time.
structuralDecisions.rationale: scope.paths for this order excludes .gitignore and index.html, which rules out the two more conventional approaches (a static <script> tag in index.html, or checking generated assets into public/ with a new .gitignore entry). Copying from node_modules/cesium/Build/Cesium at build time, rather than committing a copy, also avoids a second, driftable copy of Cesium's own asset tree in source control. Reversibility: Moderate — contained to one file, but it is the only place in this repo demonstrating the pattern, so a second consumer should extract it rather than re-derive it independently.
tradeOffs: A hand-rolled plugin is more code than a scoped dependency (e.g. vite-plugin-static-copy) would need, and nothing else in this monorepo exercises configureServer/closeBundle together — a future maintainer won't find a second example to generalize from. If a second app needs the same thing, extract this into a tiny shared Vite plugin at that point rather than copying it a third time.

Vite's dev server copies the mapping at configureServer startup, not per-request — a change to node_modules/cesium's own Build output mid-session without a dev-server restart could go unnoticed. Acceptable here since Cesium's Build output doesn't change within a single working session.

structuralDecisions.decision: Implement VITE_FEATURE_REAGENT_MAP as a single pure predicate, isReagentMapEnabled(value), with no flag service, no remote config, and no abstraction layer. This is the first VITE_FEATURE_* flag in this app and sets the convention future feature flags in this app should follow.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Matches CLAUDE.md's guidance to skip architecture-level abstraction until a second real use case demonstrates the need. A single equality check is reversible, auditable at a glance, and testable with no browser. Reversibility: Cheap.

structuralDecisions.decision: apps/ye-olde-magic-shop consumes packages/saturday-playwright-cesium's published seam contract (window.__SATURDAY_CESIUM__, saturdayMetadata) without taking any build or runtime dependency on that package. It copies the already-reviewed aurelis.jpg texture and replicates the known-good Viewer option set from fixture-globe.js as reference material only.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Keeps the two bounded contexts decoupled: this app's UI and the Test Automation package can each change internally without breaking the other, as long as both honor the documented seam contract. This is the Anti-Corruption boundary already recorded in analysis.md's crossings list. Reversibility: Cheap.

structuralDecisions.decision: Keep tests/reagent-map-*.spec.ts out of the default 'chromium' Playwright project via testIgnore, running them only under the existing 'chrome' project — reusing the project split playwright.config.ts already defines, rather than inventing a third project or a separate config file.
structuralDecisions.rationale: Cesium needs a real webgl2 context the bundled headless Chromium can't reliably provide, which is the same reason the 'chrome' project already exists in this config. Extending the existing split is simpler than a new config file, and keeps 'npm run test:e2e still passes without them' true by construction rather than by convention. Reversibility: Cheap.
